subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: Should Linux Quick Chat load arbitrary HTTP(S) identity avatar URLs by broadening the Tauri CSP, or should it remain local/data-only until OpenClaw defines an explicit remote-avatar trust policy?
rationale: This is an intentional user-visible capability with privacy and remote-content consequences; source review can identify the boundary but cannot choose the product security posture.

options.title: Keep local/data-only avatars
options.body: Do not broaden the Quick Chat image CSP; render workspace-derived data URLs and local fallback identity presentation until a remote-avatar policy is approved.

options.title: Approve remote avatars explicitly
options.body: Retain HTTP(S) avatar rendering only with documented privacy expectations and focused proof of the intended network and failure behavior.

options.title: Pause avatar rendering
options.body: Land no remote-avatar path now and split the policy-sensitive rendering decision into a narrower follow-up.

recommendation.title: Keep local/data-only avatars
recommendation.body: Do not broaden the Quick Chat image CSP; render workspace-derived data URLs and local fallback identity presentation until a remote-avatar policy is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Linux Quick Chat surface and authored both the avatar consumer and CSP change.
